things.text: SO. The Star Crystal found a farmer. Joy is a weed. I pull weeds.
things.win: The Commander's armour bursts into grey smoke. A thin, tired man stumbles out of it and runs for the hills before you can call to him. For a moment the grass under your feet turns green. Then it fades, but you remember it.
things.after: Grey ground, quiet now. Where he stood, a circle that's a little less grey than the rest.
things.text_gangsters: Every grid line out here is mine. I measured the President's tower from this dirt. I'll measure you.
things.locked: The Commander's camp is ringed with soldiers. Not yet: wake the second spark at your resonator first, and reach Combat 3.

things.text: Someone lived here when the grass was green. A child's drawing of a penguin is still pinned to the wall.

intro: Past the gate the colour drains out of the world like water out of a sink. Grey grass. Grey trees. In the middle of it a spire of black crystal, cracked with light the colour of a bruise.

intro.text: Careful. Everything here wants you to stop caring.

things.greet_spring: Mama Rosa's spring tart. One slice each.
things.greet_summer: Floats and sodas. Booth's got the fan.
things.greet_winter: Soup's on for the whole crew. Nobody eats cold on my watch.

things.text: Rooms by the night, the week, or 'until it blows over'. You look like a 'blows over'. No names in the book.
The drive-in screen is torn through. Somebody painted a crown on what's left. The President's crown. He owns the dark out here too.

intro: Hideout town. A gas station, a diner, a motel with half its sign lit, and a drive-in that stopped showing films before you were born. Everybody here is waiting for something to blow over.

things.greet: Fresh-ish. No questions about the boat.
things.greet_spring: Herring run's in. Fresh off the boats.
things.greet_fall: Mackerel weather. Buy 'em while they're cheap.
things.greet_winter: Winter cod and a few glowers. Keep your hands warm.

things.text: Warehouse three is off limits. Warehouse three has always been off limits. There is no warehouse three.
You're the farmer. The President said you'd come by water eventually. Everyone does.
things.win: He sits down hard between two containers and tosses you his jacket. 'Take it. I'm done.' In the pocket: a shipping manifest. Every crate on it is marked with a small purple crystal.
things.after: The docks are yours now. Specs says a hacker could do a lot with the harbour cameras.
things.title: Harbourmaster Vance

things.text: The ferry to the islands. Out of service since the President bought the islands.

intro: Salt, diesel, rust. Cranes like skeletons over the water. Everything that comes into the city comes through here, and somebody takes a cut of all of it.

things.greet_summer: Too hot for noodles? I got fizz.
things.greet_fall: Pumpkin broth's back. Don't ask what's in the chili.

things.greet: Sit. Eat. Nobody bothers you in here.
things.greet_winter: Winter bowl tonight. Fish stew, extra steam.
things.greet_summer: Cold noodles, cold salad. It's summer.

things.text: Manny sings here on Thursdays. Badly. Everyone comes anyway. That's what this street is: people who shouldn't, doing it anyway.
Every sign on this street answers to me. Let's see how you look lit up.
things.win: The flames go out. Under the dragon sign, a crowd that was pretending not to watch starts, very quietly, to clap.
things.after: The neon district breathes easier. Word travels to the uptown crews now.
things.locked: The neon boss is not seeing anyone who has not settled the docks.
things.title: Lucia "Flame" Ardent

things.text: Night market. Fixed prices, no haggling, no questions. Someone hand-painted a small cat in the corner.

intro: Rain on neon. Every puddle has a sign in it. Noodle steam, arcade noise, a dragon the length of a block burning pink and blue over everything.

things.text: The President sees nobody without an appointment. The President has never once made an appointment. You can see where that leaves you.
things.text_after: The doorman holds the brass door for you and looks at a point just past your ear. He has decided he never saw you.

things.text: Closed to the public. Open to the President. There's a crystal the size of a car in the vault, Specs says. Specs hacked the inventory.
Uptown doesn't do visitors. Uptown does paperwork. You're about to be filed.
things.win: The riot shield clatters down the marble steps. Behind it, for one second, the tower's doors open. Then they close. There's a slot in them like a mailbox.
things.after: The tower doors. Whatever you kept, this is where it counts.
things.locked: The tower guards look straight through you. Win the pit first; then they will take you seriously.
things.title: Silas Crane

things.text: Ticket 41. Silver coupe. Owner said 'keep it running, I'll be quick.' That was three hours ago.

things.hint: A: a coin in the hedge bed

intro: Marble, gold, trimmed hedges, and a tower that goes up until it stops being a building and becomes a threat. At the very top, something purple glows in a window.

things.text: Sparring every night: pads, gloves, and a ref who blows a whistle at anything unfriendly. The President's boys spar here too, when they want to look tough.
Forty fights. Forty wins. Nobody's knocked me down since the stone. You want to try?
things.win: The crowd roars. Sasha, at the ropes, nods once. That's all she's ever going to give anyone, and it's enough.
things.after: The pit's yours. Fighters come to you now.
things.title: Brock the Unbroken
things.locked: The pit crowd won't let you near the ring. Deal with Flame in Neon first.

things.msg: The jukebox plays something old. You breathe.

intro: Down the ladder: brick, drip, and the bass of a crowd somewhere ahead. The fight club. The only place in the city where the rules are posted.

things.text: Going north? Nobody's going north. The checkpoint's been shut since the President's people put the big head on the mountain. Vanity, that.
The checkpoint is dark. The barrier is down. The tunnel beyond it goes somewhere the map doesn't show.

things.greet: Vending machine's broke. I've got what I've got.

things.title: Old Mags
things.text: These roads are mine, sugar. The President pays me to keep them quiet. You're noisy.
things.win: Mags sits down in the road and laughs until she cries. 'He gave me a black stone and told me I'd never be old. I'm old anyway. Go on, then.'

intro: The highway out of town. Cornfields black under a purple sky, wind turbines turning, and the President's face carved into the mountain at the end of the road like he's watching you leave.

things.hint: A: climb down the great tree

things.text: An observatory. Whoever built it was looking for my kind. The telescope still points at the galaxy I fell from.
A temple with crystal columns and no roof. Carved on the floor: a paw print inside a ring of light. The Meow Pow Wow is older than penguins.

things.msg: You sit on the broken stair and the wind does the rest.

things.text: The knight lifts a sword of blue glass. Frost runs down it toward you. It hasn't spoken in twenty-one years, and it doesn't start now.
things.win: The knight's armour shatters into blue-white glass that melts into the clouds. For a moment a small grey shape stands in the frost, blinking; then it waddles off into the cloud and is gone.
things.win_reverted: The glass falls away like frost off a window. An old penguin stands where the knight was, blinking at the sky. At his feet, a crystal the size of your fist. Warm.
things.title: The Crystal Knight

intro: The stairs inside the great tree go up for a very long time, and then there is no tree, only cloud underfoot and sky in every direction. Islands float here. Something enormous swims beneath them.

things.hint: A: launch to the green planet

things.text: The bridge. Every screen shows the same thing: a planet, green and violet, and a reading that says LIFE in letters somebody underlined by hand.
Someone's asleep in these pods. Not people. Not Grumps. Something between. Don't wake them yet.

things.msg: Hydroponic strawberries. Real ones. You eat too many.

intro: The teleporter lets go of you on a metal floor that hums. Windows the size of barn doors look down on a planet. Nobody is here. Somebody was.

things.text: A statue of someone who is not a person and is not quite a penguin either, eyes closed, a crystal where the heart would be. The Star Crystal goes very quiet.
A crashed ship, old, overgrown. The markings on the hull are the same ones that are on the Star Crystal.

things.msg: The giant flower opens and closes once, slowly, and the air is sweet.

intro: Teal moss, violet earth, mushrooms the size of houses glowing from the inside. Fireflies that are not fireflies. Everything here breathes.
Hills that roll like a shaken blanket, and every hill wears an orchard. Bees. A windmill turning slow against the sky. Someone is whistling to a dog.

lines: Sheep don't care what season it is. Neither do I, much.
Apples are in the basket by the hut. Help yourself, pay what you like.
The dog found something in the far orchard. Wouldn't let me see.

things.msg: A hot spring in the rocks. The cold leaves your bones.

things.text: The ranger's lookout. From here you can see the sea, the lake, and your own chimney.

things.hint: A: something growing between the stones

intro: Thin air, pale grass, snow in the shadows even in summer. An eagle turns overhead. The valley is a green bowl far below.

things.text: Six stones in a ring, one fallen. The carvings are the same spiral that the crystal makes when it dreams.

things.hint: A: coins in the statue's hand

things.text: An arch that leads nowhere. Walk through it and your ears pop.
The guardian statue's runes light one by one. Sel: 'I told you not to touch the—' It steps off its plinth.
things.win: The Warden kneels, runes dark, and becomes a statue again. In its hand: a blade older than the town.
things.after: The Warden, kneeling. Sel sketches it from a safe distance.
things.title: The Ruin Warden

intro: Nobody built this, the town says. Nobody remembers. Moss on the pillars, and something under the moss that still glows a little at night.

lines: The spiral is the same as the one the crystal dreams. I've checked.
Don't touch the fallen stone. I did. My ears haven't stopped.
Theo thinks I'm making it up. Theo has never been here after dark.
lines_gangsters: The spiral is carved on the President's tower doors too. I've checked. Twice.
Don't touch the fallen stone. I did. My ears haven't stopped.
Theo thinks I'm making it up. Theo has never been here after dark.

intro: The old stones keep a secret the town forgot: smugglers have a hideaway under them. Crates where the altar was, lanterns in the arches, and someone watching from the dark.

things.text: The old crane. Chains rusted stiff. A sign: GRANITE & SONS — BACK AFTER LUNCH. The lunch was some years ago.
The foreman's tower. Someone still sweeps it.
The biggest stone in the quarry opens its eyes. Crystals crown it. It remembers being carved.
things.win: The Golem King crumbles into ore. Granite watches from the tower and doesn't say anything for a long time.
things.after: A ring of fresh ore where the king stood.
things.title: The Golem King

intro: The quarry: a bowl of cut stone, terraces like giant steps, rails that go nowhere now. The ore is still in the walls. Nobody has told the golems the work stopped.

lines: Work stopped. Ore didn't.
Bring me coal and I'll fire the old crane up. Maybe.
Golems were the crew's idea. Carve a stone man to lift stone. What could go wrong.

intro: Granite & Sons, says the sign. Nobody named Granite has worked here in years. The crew that runs it now cuts more deals than stone, and the floodlights never go off.

things.hint: A: something sticky in the log

things.text: The black water boils. Something that was a woman once stands up out of it, reeds for hair, a lantern that isn't lit by fire.
things.win: The witch sinks back into the bog, laughing, and comes up far off in the reeds, small and tired, and the fog goes with her. Old Moss will want to hear about this.
things.after: The bog where the witch rose. Still.
things.title: The Marsh Witch

intro: Mud that sucks at your boots, black water, cattails taller than you. Frogs stop singing when you pass and start again behind you. Lights move out there that aren't lanterns.

lines: Don't drink the black water. Not even if it asks nicely.
The wisps are only curious. Mostly.
Frogs know things. I listen.

intro: Black water, tall reeds, and an airboat landing nobody admits to building. Smugglers run crates through here at night, and the frogs have learned to go quiet when the engines start.

things.hint: A: a bucket in the boat

things.msg: Fish on the fire. Someone left it for whoever came by.

intro: Three rivers braid through sand bars and willow. Otters. Herons standing like they've been there since the valley was made. The lake is downstream, the marsh up.

battle.title: Frostfield Front
battle.brief: The Dark Crystal's grumps hold the high ground over Frostfield. Take the ridges, raise crystal spires, and push them off the plateaus.
battle.win: Frostfield breathes again. The spires hum like a choir that finally found its note.
battle.lose: Back to camp. The ridges will still be there tomorrow.

battle.title: Shattered Vale
battle.brief: The Vale broke when the Dark Crystal fell through it. Its shards still march. Hold the six points and the shards will stop answering it.
battle.win: The shards in the Vale go quiet, then warm. Some of them follow your spires home.
battle.lose: The Vale is too loud today. Rest and come back.

battle.title: The Rail Yards
battle.brief: The President's people run the freight through the rail yards. Take the towers, set up drone bays, and the trains run for you.
battle.win: The yard's yours. The night freight blows its whistle twice as it passes your boxcar.
battle.lose: Pull back to the boxcar. We regroup.

battle.title: Dockside War
battle.brief: The docks are where the President's money comes in. Six points, four of his crews. Bring drones, bring the crew, and hold the water.
battle.win: The harbour lights come on one by one, and every one of them is yours.
battle.lose: The tide's against us. Back to the trawler.

things.empty: Just sand and a crab, now.

things.text: A carving on a flat stone: four crystals in a ring around a fifth. Under it, in merkitty scratch-script: 'Pink for the morning. Ask the others for the rest.'

intro: Pink stilt-huts, grey coral creeping up the beach, and somewhere a merkitty singing, badly out of tune.

things.empty: Only kelp and a cross little crab.

things.text: Kelp stems pressed into the mud in a spiral, like a star map drawn by someone falling. A shell is pinned at the centre: 'Green for the forest. Brine has the morning.'

things.empty: The fog will wash more up.

intro: Teal moss down to the waterline, huts leaning on kelp-wrapped legs, and fog that moves like it's breathing.

things.text: Words scratched into the ice by a claw, still sharp: 'White for the winter. We were one star, once. Ask Cinderpaw how it ends.'

things.empty: Someone's taken the coal for the hearths. Fair.

intro: Snow on everything, the lodge chimneys barely smoking, and a frozen shoreline creaking like an old door.

things.empty: Sand gone to glass, then gone to someone's pocket.

things.text: A tile of black glass with gold in it: four flames in a ring around a fifth, dark one. 'Gold for the fire. And four become one.'

things.empty: The mountain will cough up more.

intro: Black sand, warm underfoot, glassworks glowing along the shore, and over it all a mountain that won't stop grumbling.

things.text: Carved into the rock by the lift, in a hand older than the town: WHERE THE STAR WAS BORN, IT STILL BEATS.
A miner's journal, waterlogged: "Day 40. The light down here isn't from the crystals. The crystals are from the light."
A painted wall: a falling star, a field, two small figures, and a long line of people carrying pieces of it away.

things.hint: A: a crystal growing out of the moss
A: a blue glint in the wall
A: something round in a nest of roots

things.text: The geode splits like an egg. What climbs out has no face, only a hunger shaped like light, and it turns toward the warmth in your pocket.
things.win: It folds in on itself and goes out, the way a candle does. In the empty geode, something beats: slow, steady, warm. The Heart.
things.after: The empty geode. Something inside still beats.
things.title: The Last Keeper

lines: You came down all hundred and fifty. Of course you did.
Every rune I've ever read points here.
The Heart isn't a place. It's a someone.

intro: The lift goes down past where the rope should run out, and then it stops, and there is a whole country under the world.
Moss that glows teal, rivers that run with light, mushrooms as tall as houses, and far off, in a geode the size of the town hall, something beating like a heart.

battle.title: The Orchard Line
battle.brief: Grumps have dug in among the apple rows. Take the press and the granary and the orchard is ours again.
battle.win: The orchard rows are quiet. Somebody's already picking apples.
battle.lose: Back to the wagons. The apples will keep.

battle.title: Bog Crossing
battle.brief: The bog has more mouths than paths. Hold the causeways and the reeds, and the mire lets you through.
battle.win: The fog lifts off the bog like a lid. The frogs start singing again.
battle.lose: The mire wins today. Back to the rafts.

battle.title: The Ashen Flats
battle.brief: Nothing grows on the Ashen Flats but trouble. Take the gate and the watchtower and the wind changes.
battle.win: The ash settles. Under it, something green is already trying.
battle.lose: Pull back to the lanterns. The flats aren't going anywhere.

battle.title: The Neon Block
battle.brief: Every sign on this block belongs to the President's crews. Switch them off one by one and the street is yours.
battle.win: The block hums under your colours. The night market reopens before you've even left.
battle.lose: Too hot tonight. Back to the van.

battle.title: Highland Pass
battle.brief: The highland pass climbs in steps of stone and snow. Hold the cairns and the ridge, and the high road is yours.
battle.win: The pass is open. Somewhere a goat bell rings like it's cheering.
battle.lose: The wind wins this one. Back down to camp.

battle.title: The Deep Cut
battle.brief: The quarry's terraces ring a deep pit. Take the cranes and the high terrace, and the golems lose their footing.
battle.win: The cranes swing your way. The golems set down their hammers.
battle.lose: Too much rock, too few friends. Back to the gate.

battle.title: The River Ford
battle.brief: The river splits the field in two. Cross at the fords, take the weir, and the far bank falls.
battle.win: The weir opens and the river runs easy. Fish leap all the way upstream.
battle.lose: The river's against us today. Back to the ferry.

battle.title: The Pillared Court
battle.brief: An old court of pillars around a raised dais. The guardians hold the dais; take the colonnades and climb.
battle.win: The guardians bow their stone heads. The court is quiet and warm in the sun.
battle.lose: The stones are stubborn today. Back to the stair.

battle.title: The Cloud Stair
battle.brief: Up here the ground is cloud and the walls are sky. Hold the star pillars and the grumps fall back down the stair.
battle.win: The clouds part under your feet. The pillars hum a bright, clean note.
battle.lose: Too high, too windy. Back to the summit camp.

battle.title: Station Deck
battle.brief: The station's decks circle a dark reactor ring. Shards crawl the corridors; take the wings and power it back up.
battle.win: The deck lights come on one row at a time. Somebody left the radio playing.
battle.lose: The air's thin and the shards are thick. Back to the dock.

battle.title: Glowroot Grove
battle.brief: A glowing river cuts the grove. Shards hold the far bank; cross on the roots and take the temple.
battle.win: The giant flowers turn to watch you pass, and they seem pleased.
battle.lose: The jungle closes in. Back to the landing.

battle.title: Reef Shallows
battle.brief: A tidal channel splits the reef. Wade the sandbars, take the coral arch, and the colony can see you coming.
battle.win: The merkitties wave from the shore. The reef glows pink and gold.
battle.lose: The tide turns. Back to the boats.

battle.title: Kelp Beds
battle.brief: Kelp and black water everywhere. Hold the dry humps between the pools and light a path to the colony.
battle.win: The kelp sways open. Little lights blink on all along the path.
battle.lose: The eels have the water today. Back to the raft.

battle.title: Fountain Plaza
battle.brief: Uptown's plaza rings a raised fountain terrace. The guards hold the terrace; take the lawns and walk up.
battle.win: The fountain's yours. Up close the tower looks smaller.
battle.lose: Too many suits on the lawn. Back to the terrace.

battle.title: The Sewer Works
battle.brief: The sewer works run along one long channel. Crawlers and crews hold the outfalls; cross the walkways and take the pumps.
battle.win: The pumps thump in time. Down here your name echoes.
battle.lose: It stinks and they know it. Back up the ladder.

intro: Roz throws a line round a post: 'The Shoals. Shallow, warm, full of fish. Cast anywhere.'
Roz kills the engine. 'Blue Deep. Mind the fog. The big ones come up at night.'

things.greet: Moth-light, glow-jam, things that hum. What'll it be?

things.msg: You dip your hands in the glowing pond. Everything aches a little less.

things.text: Lantern board: 'Violet Glade, north. Crystal Thicket, east. The Moonpool is past the glade, and the Thornmother sleeps under it. Please don't wake her. (Someone has written underneath: SOMEONE HAS TO.)'

npcs.name: Liesl
lines: Every lantern here has a moth, and every moth has a name. That one's Bartholomew.
The Thornmother wasn't always thorns. Once she was the garden.
Wisp Sparks keep a pudding light. Bring one back and cook something nice.
lines_gangsters: Every lantern here has a moth, and every moth has a name. That one's Bartholomew.
Rosa Thorne says the garden pays her rent. The garden has never paid anyone anything.
Wisp Sparks keep a pudding light. Bring one back and cook something nice.
after: The garden's breathing again. Bartholomew's taken to sleeping in the roses.
Every lantern here has a moth, and every moth has a name. That one's Bartholomew.
after_gangsters: Nobody collects rent in Lanternfall now. Bartholomew's moved into the roses.
Every lantern here has a moth, and every moth has a name. That one's Bartholomew.

npcs.name: Fenn
lines: Glowmoss grows on the north side of everything. Even me, if I stand still.
The Crystal Thicket chimes when the wind's right.
Honey and wisp-light. That's the trick to a Gloam Pudding.

npcs.name: Bramble
lines: Did you see the giant flower? It sneezed on me.
I'm not scared of the dark. The dark is scared of my lantern.
The ghostfish in the Moonpool can see you even with their eyes closed.
after: The giant flower stopped sneezing. I sort of miss it.
I'm not scared of the dark. The dark is scared of my lantern.

intro: The ring lets go of you in a hush of moth-wings. Lanterns everywhere, hung from mushrooms taller than houses, and the moss underfoot is violet and soft.
This is Lanternfall. Somebody waves. Somebody is always waving here.

things.hint: A: a spark caught in a web
A: a moth asleep on a cap
A: glowing caps in a ring

things.text: A stone, carved with roots: 'The Glade remembers every footstep. Walk kindly.'

intro: Teal moss up to your ankles and flowers that open as you pass. The Glade breathes in when you breathe out.

things.hint: A: sparks humming in the crystals

things.text: The crystals ring a note when you touch them. Touch them in a row and it's almost a song. Almost the song Liesl hums.

intro: Crystal grass, crystal trees, a wind that rings like a hundred tiny bells. Every step is a chord.

things.title: The Thornmother
things.text: Thorns uncoil from the dark water and stand up into a shape like a woman made of brambles. 'Another one who walks on my garden,' she whispers.
things.win: The thorns loosen and fall away, and for a moment there is only an old gardener, very tired, smiling. Then there is only a rose by the water, and a bud closed tight.
things.after: A single rose grows by the water. It turns to follow you, gently.
things.locked: The moonpool is still and black, and something among the roses is waiting. Help Liesl in Lanternfall first.
things.text_gangsters: A woman in a thorn-green coat steps out from behind the roses, pruning shears in one hand. 'This garden pays me rent,' says Rosa Thorne. 'Everyone in Gloamwood pays me rent.'
things.win_gangsters: Rosa snips one rose, tucks it in your collar and backs off into the mist. 'Fine. The garden's yours. Water it.' Nobody in Lanternfall pays her again.
things.after_gangsters: The roses grow wild again. Nobody collects rent here now.

things.msg: Moonlight off the water settles on you like a blanket.
things.hint: A: sit by the moonlit water

things.text: An old garden sign, nearly swallowed by thorns: 'MOTHER'S GARDEN. PLEASE DO NOT PICK THE ROSES. SHE WILL KNOW.'

intro: Mist on black water, and a moon in it that isn't the moon in the sky. Somewhere under the thorns something is sleeping very lightly.

things.greet: Shade, water, and whatever the caravans dropped off. Look around.

things.msg: Cold well water, the best thing you've ever tasted.

things.text: Caravan board: 'DUNE SEA west. GLASS CANYON north, and past it the SUNKEN TEMPLE, where the Colossus guards the door. Water before you go. Water after you go.'

npcs.name: Sefa
lines: The dunes move a little every night. The map moves with them.
Desert Saffron grows where the crabs dig. Funny, that.
Sun Loaf keeps three days in a saddlebag. Learned that the hard way.

npcs.name: Rahim
lines: Fifty years at this well. Never once seen it run dry.
The temple builders drew suns on everything. Even the spoons.
Bring me sunstones and I'll pay you in shade. And something better than shade.
done_lines: The lamps burn till dawn now. Caravans come in singing.
Fifty years at this well. Never once seen it run dry.

npcs.name: Nadia
lines: The Colossus isn't evil. It's a guard that nobody told the war was over.
The Glass Canyon was a lake once. Lightning turned the sand to glass.
I'd give a lot for a scarab from the temple. For science.
lines_gangsters: The Glass Canyon was a lake once. Lightning turned the sand to glass.
Vasco sits on a crate of temple gold and calls himself a king. The scarabs were kings first.
I'd give a lot for a scarab from the temple. For science.
done_lines: The scarab's a calendar. I've read three months of it. Next month has a festival.
The Glass Canyon was a lake once. Lightning turned the sand to glass.
after: The Colossus is sleeping. Someone finally told it the war was over. You did.
after_gangsters: Vasco's crate sits empty. I'm reading the temple walls at last.

intro: The caravan rolls in under a white sky. Tents, a stone well, palms leaning over a little green oasis, and beyond it nothing but gold in every direction.
Mirage Post. The last well before the Sunscorch Expanse.

things.hint: A: something glints in the sand

things.text: A sign, sand-scoured almost blank: '...ASIS 2 DAYS. DO NOT FOLLOW THE SINGING.'

intro: Dunes like frozen waves, as far as you can see. Somewhere out here a bus is half buried, and something under the sand is singing.

things.hint: A: lightning glass in the sand

things.msg: A little spring in the rock, cold and clear.
things.hint: A: a spring in the rock

things.text: Carved over the canyon path: a sun, a giant with a spear, and rows of tiny people bowing. Someone has added a moustache to the giant.

intro: Red rock walls and a floor of sand fused into glass in long, lightning-shaped streaks. It crunches. The golems here are made of it.

things.title: The Sun Colossus
things.text: Sand pours off a giant of gold stone as it stands. Its spear comes down across the doorway. 'NONE PASS UNTIL THE SUN RETURNS.'
things.win: The Colossus kneels, slowly, and the light behind its eyes turns from white to warm. 'The sun... has returned,' it says, looking at you. It sits down to rest for the first time in a thousand years.
things.after: The Colossus sits by the door, at peace, sun on its face.
things.locked: Sand has buried the temple door to the lintel. Help Nadia in Mirage Post, and the dunes will shift.
things.text_gangsters: A big man in a sun-bleached coat sits on a crate of temple gold in the doorway. 'Every caravan pays the Dune King,' says Vasco. 'You're a caravan now.'
things.win_gangsters: Vasco climbs off the crate, dusts himself down and laughs. 'Keep the door, then. The sand was getting in my boots anyway.' He leaves the temple to the scholars.
things.after_gangsters: Vasco's crate sits empty by the door. The caravans pass for free.

things.hint: A: a gold scarab in a niche

things.text: A tablet: 'THE SUN SET ITS GUARD AT THE DOOR AND SAID: KEEP THEM OUT UNTIL I RETURN. THE SUN DID NOT RETURN.'
Runes glow faintly as you pass. They spell, as far as you can tell, 'WELCOME'. Then, smaller: 'MOSTLY'.

intro: Half buried in sand, a temple of pale stone. Braziers still burn at the far door, and something enormous is sitting very still in front of it.

things.greet: Coffee's hot, stew's hotter. Cash only, sugar.

things.msg: You sit a while and watch the trains not come. It's nicer than it sounds.

things.text: Timetable, all trains CANCELLED by order of BARON COALBROOK. Underneath, in chalk: 'FREIGHT YARDS WEST. MILL NORTH. THE BARON HIDES IN THE TUNNELS PAST THE MILL. SOMEBODY DO SOMETHING.'

npcs.name: Hollis
lines: Every rail in this valley runs through Junction. That's why the Baron wants it.
Rail Chain, Engine Oil, Tin. Junction runs on all three.
My engine's the last one he hasn't bought. She stays mine.
after: Baron's gone and the trains run on time. Well. Mostly on time. On a time.
My engine's the last one he never bought. She stays mine.

npcs.name: Dot
lines: You want the stew? Everybody wants the stew.
Charcoal from the firebox, that's the secret. Smoky.
The Baron eats here. Tips terribly.
after: The Baron's table is free now. Nobody wants it. Too many bad tips in the wood.

npcs.name: Skip
lines: Paper! Baron cancels all trains! Read all about it!
I sold a paper to a rail bot once. It tried to eat it.
The tunnels go under the whole city. I've seen like, half.
after: Paper! Trains run again! Read all about it! ...I wrote that one myself.

intro: The night train screeches into Junction City under a sky the colour of an old penny. Coal smoke, brick, and every timetable on the station wall says CANCELLED.
Somebody here runs the rails. Somebody here is about to have a very bad week.

things.hint: A: chain on a broken coupling

things.text: A shipping manifest: '400 crates TIN to BARON. 300 crates COAL to BARON. 1 crate TEDDY BEARS to BARON (personal).'

intro: Rows of rusting freight cars, cranes like skeletons, and rail bots patrolling with lanterns. All of it stamped COALBROOK.

things.msg: A fire barrel and a crate to sit on. Warm hands, warm heart.
things.hint: A: warm up at the barrel

things.text: A poster: 'WORK HARDER. THE BARON IS WATCHING.' Someone has drawn him a very small hat.

intro: Brick mills with every window lit, chimneys coughing, and a great silo with the Baron's crest painted on it twice as tall as a house.

things.title: Baron Coalbrook
things.text: A man in a coal-black coat steps off a private rail car and checks a gold pocket watch. 'You're eight minutes late for your own defeat.'
things.win: The Baron sits down hard on his own rail car. 'Fine. FINE. The trains can run.' He hands over the watch. 'It's eight minutes fast. It always was.'
things.after: The Baron's rail car, empty. A timetable on the seat reads: ALL TRAINS RUNNING.
things.locked: The private platform is roped off: NO PASSENGERS. Help Hollis in Junction City first, and you'll get a ticket.

things.hint: A: the Baron's petty cash box

things.text: The Baron's ledger: every station, every rail, every penny of Ironline, and in the margin, 'buy the moon??'

intro: Under the mills the old rail tunnels run in the dark, lamps flickering along the walls. Far ahead, a private rail car is parked with all its lights on.

things.greet: Warm things for cold people. Everything's knitted, even the sorbet. Not really.

things.msg: You sink into the hot spring up to your chin. Somewhere a snowflake lands on your nose and gives up.

things.text: Guide's board: 'GLACIER FIELDS north, then the SUMMIT. RIME CAVERNS west. FROZEN FALLS east, good fishing. Something big sleeps on the Summit. Don't sing near it.'

npcs.name: Brannoch
lines: Hearthhold's been here as long as the snow. Longer, some say.
Rime Crystal won't melt in a forge. Freeze it into a sorbet instead.
The Wyrm on the Summit wakes every hundred years. Lucky you.
lines_gangsters: Hearthhold's been here as long as the snow. Longer, some say.
Rime Crystal won't melt in a forge. Freeze it into a sorbet instead.
Big Ike hauls ice off the Summit and sells it back to us. Our own ice.
after: The Wyrm's snoring again. Hearthhold sleeps easier for it.
Rime Crystal won't melt in a forge. Freeze it into a sorbet instead.
after_gangsters: Big Ike's sled tracks go down the mountain and don't come back. Good.
Rime Crystal won't melt in a forge. Freeze it into a sorbet instead.

npcs.name: Ingrid
lines: Edelweiss, milk and a Rime Crystal. That's a sorbet that never melts.
My grandmother knitted the first igloo. Don't ask how.
Glacier Glass makes the best windows. You can see next week through it.

npcs.name: Tove
lines: I named the pike in the falls. They're all called Pike.
The caverns sing when the wind goes through. I sing back.
Brannoch says I can go to the Summit when I'm nine hundred.
after: Brannoch says I can go to the Summit now. When I'm nine hundred and one.

intro: The sled tips you out in front of a village of snow-domed houses with smoke curling from every chimney. Lanterns on poles, a steaming spring, and the peaks all round like a crown.
Hearthhold. Even the snow seems friendly here.

things.hint: A: a sheet of clear ice
A: edelweiss in the lee of a rock

things.text: A cairn with a plaque: 'FOR THE CLIMBERS WHO TURNED BACK. YOU WERE RIGHT.'

intro: White in every direction, blue in the cracks. The glacier groans under you like a very old dog getting comfortable.

things.hint: A: a frozen pane in the wall

things.text: A journal frozen into the ice, readable through it: 'The caverns hum the same note as the Summit. I think the Wyrm is snoring.'

intro: Blue ice overhead, blue ice underfoot, and your breath hangs in the air like it's afraid to leave. The walls hum one long, low note.

things.hint: A: a pike frozen in the edge ice

things.msg: The falls roar under the ice. Somehow it's peaceful.

things.text: Fishing log, Tove (age 8): 'Monday: Pike. Tuesday: Pike. Wednesday: a different Pike.'

intro: A waterfall frozen halfway down, still pouring under its skin of ice. The pools below are open and dark, and full of pike.

things.title: The Rime Wyrm
things.text: The snowfield shrugs. A head as long as a sled lifts out of the ice, frost pouring from its jaws, and two pale eyes open. It is not pleased to be awake.
things.win: The Wyrm sighs a long, cold sigh and curls back down into the snow. Before it sleeps it drops one scale at your feet, as if to say: fine. You win. Now let me sleep.
things.after: The snow over the Wyrm rises and falls, slowly. It's snoring.
things.locked: The snowfield above is quiet. Too quiet. Help Ingrid in Hearthhold before you climb.
things.text_gangsters: A sled the size of a truck, and on it a man the size of the sled. 'Nobody hauls ice off this mountain but Big Ike,' he says, cracking his knuckles.
things.win_gangsters: Big Ike sits down in the snow, out of breath. 'All right, all right. The summit's free. Hearthhold can have its ice.' He slides off down the mountain.
things.after_gangsters: Sled tracks lead down the mountain. Big Ike doesn't haul here any more.

things.text: A ragged flag on a pole. Under it, a tin with notes from everyone who made it. The newest says: 'SHHH. IT'S SLEEPING.'

things.hint: A: a nest in the snow
things.wait: A hollow in the snow, warm somehow. Whatever owns it is up on the summit, and not in the mood.
things.line: Something small and sleepy blinks up at you from the snow hollow, and follows you all the way down. Ingrid will bring it to your farm.
things.line_gang: An old tortoise sits in the warm hollow, frost on its shell, very patient. It follows you, slowly. Ingrid will truck it to your place.

intro: The top of the world. Wind like knives, sky like glass, and in the middle of the snowfield a long shape under the snow, breathing.

things.greet: Feathers, fluff, and food that floats! Mind it doesn't float off.

things.msg: You lie back on a cloud. It's exactly as comfortable as you always hoped.

things.text: Wind vane board: 'SUNRISE SHELF west, gentle. STORM SHELF north, not gentle. STARFALL GARDEN past the storm, where the Roc nests. Hold on to your hat. Hold on to your penguin.'

npcs.name: Zephyr
lines: Breezehaven! Where penguins fly, technically, in baskets.
Storm Glass comes from where lightning lands. Don't be where lightning lands.
The Roc thinks the whole sky is its nest. It isn't wrong.
after: The sky's ours again. Well, the Roc's, but it shares now.
Storm Glass comes from where lightning lands. Don't be where lightning lands.

npcs.name: Gull
lines: There's a cloud pool on Sunrise Shelf. Skyfin bite there at dawn.
Storm Fluff makes a souffle rise like a cloud. Because it is one.
I came up in a balloon forty years ago. Never found the way down. Never looked.

npcs.name: Nimbus
lines: The Star Crystal's light reaches all the way up here. The clouds love it.
The Storm Shelf was calm, once. The Roc changed that.
Bring me Storm Glass and I'll teach you to bottle a breeze. Well. Pay you, anyway.
done_lines: I bottled a breeze. It got out. It's somewhere in the gondola now, being smug.
The Storm Shelf is calm again. The clouds have stopped flinching.

intro: The balloon drifts up through the last cloud and into blue. Islands float in it like stepping stones, one with a windmill, one with a temple, one with a penguin waving both flippers.
Breezehaven. The wind here smells of rain that hasn't happened yet.

things.hint: A: a tuft of storm cloud
A: dust from a falling star

things.text: A stone that floats, carved: 'FIRST LIGHT FALLS HERE FIRST.' The carving glows faintly pink.

intro: Pink cloud and gold light. The Shelf is always just at sunrise, no matter what time it is down below.

things.hint: A: storm fluff snagged on a rod

things.text: A sign, scorched: 'DO NOT STAND HERE DURING STORMS. (IT IS ALWAYS STORMING.)'

intro: Black cloud underfoot, lightning in it like veins. The rods hum. Your hair stands up and crackles.

things.title: The Storm Roc
things.text: Wings like thunderheads open over the garden. The Roc lands, and every star in the garden flickers. It screams once, and the wind screams with it.
things.win: The Roc folds its wings and the storm goes with them. It looks at you, then at the Star Crystal's glow, and bows its great head. A feather drifts down, crackling.
things.after: The Roc's nest, empty and peaceful. A breeze, just a breeze.
things.locked: The garden gate is held shut by a wind you can lean on. Help Nimbus in Breezehaven first.

things.hint: A: a crater full of glitter
A: something perfectly calm in a nest
A: a ring of soft down
things.wait: A ring of soft down, crackling with static. Something huge sleeps nearby. Not yet.
things.line: A young roc, no bigger than a goose, tumbles out of the down and peeps at you. It's decided you're family. Nimbus will walk it down to your farm.

things.msg: Starlight in the garden settles on you. You feel very small, and very fine.

things.text: A star chart, with one star circled again and again: the one that fell on the valley. Next to it: 'IT'S COMING HOME.'

intro: Above the storm, the sky goes dark and full of stars, close enough to touch. Flowers glow in the cloud. In the middle of it all, a nest the size of a barn.

things.greet: Only the finest. Prices on request. Requests are discouraged.

things.msg: You sit on the fountain's edge. The spray is cool and smells faintly of money.

things.text: Brass plaque: 'GILT CITY. CASINO ROW east, and beneath it THE VAULTS. GILDED GARDENS west. By order of MADAME AURUM, everything here is hers. Including this plaque.'

npcs.name: Pell
lines: Madame owns the casinos, the gardens, the Vaults, and the fountain. The water is rented.
Collectors pay well for Gilt Chips. The Gilded Ace on the Row takes cash only.
She'll see you in the Vaults. She sees everyone in the Vaults, eventually.
after: Madame's left the Vaults. The fountain water's free. I'm still not used to it.

npcs.name: Odette
lines: I paint the statues. Madame keeps asking me to make them look more like her.
Gold leaf on a flan. Disgusting. Delicious.
The gardens are the only place in Gilt City that's free. Don't tell her.
after: I'm painting the statues to look like whoever I like now. Mostly pigeons.

npcs.name: Cass
lines: Fastest legs in Gilt. Madame's guards can't catch me.
There's a lucky coin under every third bench. I've checked.
I'd steal her crown, but it's glued on.
after: Nobody's chasing me any more. It's honestly a bit dull.

intro: The limousine purrs into a plaza paved with gold-veined stone. Statues, fountains, a mansion with a hundred windows, and every lamp post has a little crown on top.
Gilt City. Everything glitters. Everything has a price.

things.text: The Neon Hotel. A brass sign: ROOMS FOR GUESTS OF THE GILDED ACE. Tonight every room is booked; the desk clerk points you across the Row to the casino.

things.hint: A: a coin in the fountain

things.text: House rules: 1. The house always wins. 2. See rule 1. 3. No running. (Someone has crossed out 3 and written CASS WAS HERE.)

intro: Neon on gold. Every door is a casino, every window shows somebody winning, and none of them look happy about it.

things.hint: A: something shining in the hedge

things.msg: A bench under a rose arch. The only free thing in Gilt City.

things.text: Gardener's note: 'Madame wants the roses gold. Roses do not come in gold. I have explained this nine times.'

intro: Hedges clipped into crowns, roses in perfect rows, gold-fish in gold ponds. Even the bees look expensive.

things.title: Madame Aurum
things.text: A woman in gold steps out from between the stacks, crown glittering. 'So you're the one my car's been driving about. Let's see what you're worth.'
things.win: Madame Aurum laughs, actually laughs, and sits on a pile of coins. 'Oh, I like you. Keep the ring. The Vaults can spare it. And the gardens are yours to wander, free.'
things.after: Madame Aurum's stack of coins. She left a note: 'Dinner? Bring the flan.'
things.locked: The vault doors are shut and the guards won't look at you. Help Odette in the Grand Plaza first.

things.hint: A: a stack of gold leaf

things.text: Vault ledger: 'Gold: yes. Pearls: yes. Friends: (blank).'

intro: Under the casinos, the Vaults: gold in stacks to the ceiling, fences of gold, and the soft tick of somebody counting.

things.hint: A: a crystal glowing in the moss
A: blooms by the glowing water
A: a soft light in the moss
things.line: A glowworm curls round your finger and won't let go. It wants to see the sky. It'll be at your farm by morning.
things.line_gang: A little gecko with a battery-blue glow skitters up your sleeve. Somebody's lab lost it. It's yours now.

things.msg: You sit by the glowing water. The light goes right through you, warm.

things.text: A miners' slate, chalk still sharp: 'Camp 9. Water here glows. Drank it. Feel fine. Feel BETTER than fine. Do not tell the foreman.'
An old map pinned to a crate: the Heart in the middle, and around it a ring of caverns marked 'DEEPS', 'DEEPER', and one just marked 'NO'.

intro: East of the Heart the caverns open into rivers of light: crystal floors, glowing pools, and the cold ashes of a miners' camp nobody ever came back for.

things.hint: A: dust shaken off a passing whale
A: a curl of storm cloud

things.msg: The whale's song rolls through the cloud. You feel lighter.

things.text: Carved into a floating stone: 'THE WHALE IS NOT LOST. IT IS WAITING FOR SOMEONE WHO WILL LISTEN.'

intro: Above the Cloud Isles the air thins and sings. A shadow the size of a town slides under the clouds below you: the sky whale, circling, circling.
